For \(n=pq\) with distinct primes \(p<q\), we need exactly three divisors less than \(15\). Since \(1<15\), this requires \(p,q<15\) and \(pq\ge 15\). The valid products are
\[
22,26,15,21,33,39,35,55,65,77,91,143.
\]
Their sum is
\[
622.
\]

For \(n=p^3\), only \(3^3=27\) works because its divisors are \(1,3,9,27\).

Thus the total sum is
\[
622+27=\boxed{649}.
\]
